events.title: David Chaum Proposed Cryptographic Electronic Money
events.description: David Chaum introduced the concept of cryptographically protected electronic money, which later influenced the development of digital currencies.

events.title: DigiCash Was Founded
events.description: David Chaum founded DigiCash, a company focused on developing cryptographic electronic money.

events.title: e-gold Was Founded
events.description: e-gold launched as one of the first online digital payment systems, preparing the way for later cryptocurrency adoption.

events.title: CyberCash Launched
events.description: CyberCash introduced a digital payment platform that demonstrated the commercial potential of online payment systems.

events.title: Hashcash Was Proposed
events.description: Adam Back proposed Hashcash, a proof-of-work mechanism that later influenced Bitcoin's mining model.

events.title: B-Money Was Proposed
events.description: Wei Dai published the B-money proposal, describing a decentralized digital currency and distributed accounting model.

events.title: e-gold Became a Major Digital Payment Service
events.description: e-gold gained major attention as an early digital money platform used for online commerce and transfers.

events.title: Bit Gold Was Proposed
events.description: Nick Szabo described Bit Gold, a concept for a decentralized digital currency secured by cryptographic proof.

events.title: Reusable Proofs of Work Were Created
events.description: Hal Finney developed Reusable Proofs of Work, one of the direct technical precursors to Bitcoin.

events.title: Bitcoin Concept Gained Wider Attention
events.description: The cryptography and digital money communities increasingly explored the idea of peer-to-peer electronic cash systems.

events.title: The Bitcoin Project Began to Take Shape
events.description: Satoshi Nakamoto and a growing online community developed the technical and social foundation of Bitcoin.

events.title: Bitcoin.org Was Registered
events.description: The bitcoin.org domain was registered and later became the primary website for Bitcoin discussion and software distribution.

events.title: The Bitcoin Whitepaper Was Published
events.description: Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin whitepaper, explaining a peer-to-peer electronic cash system.

events.title: The Bitcoin Genesis Block Was Mined
events.description: Satoshi Nakamoto mined the first Bitcoin block, known as the Genesis Block.

events.title: The First Bitcoin Transaction Took Place
events.description: Hal Finney received 10 BTC from Satoshi Nakamoto during the network's early testing phase.

events.title: Bitcoin Mining Began in Earnest
events.description: Early miners began securing the network and validating transactions as the Bitcoin blockchain grew.

events.title: The First Bitcoin Nodes Started Running
events.description: The early Bitcoin network began to function as a distributed peer-to-peer system.

events.title: Bitcoin Was First Mentioned in Public Media
events.description: Bitcoin began attracting attention beyond cryptography circles as early news coverage emerged.

events.title: Bitcoin Market Value Began Growing
events.description: The Bitcoin ecosystem started to show early signs of exchange trading and user adoption.

events.title: Bitcoin Pizza Day
events.description: Laszlo Hanyecz paid 10,000 BTC for two pizzas, an event that became a symbol of Bitcoin's early utility.

events.title: Mt. Gox Was Founded
events.description: Mt. Gox was founded as a Bitcoin exchange and later became the largest exchange in the early market.

events.title: Bitcoin Reached One Dollar
events.description: Bitcoin's price began gaining real-world value as exchange trading expanded.

events.title: Litecoin Was Launched
events.description: Charlie Lee launched Litecoin, a Bitcoin-inspired cryptocurrency with a different mining algorithm.

events.title: Namecoin Was Launched
events.description: Namecoin introduced a blockchain-based naming system and demonstrated non-financial blockchain use cases.

events.title: Bitcoin Reached 10 Dollars
events.description: Bitcoin's price passed the $10 threshold, marking a major increase in market recognition.

events.title: Ripple Labs Was Founded
events.description: Ripple Labs developed a payment-focused blockchain network that later became a major digital asset ecosystem.

events.title: Coinbase Was Founded
events.description: Coinbase was founded to make Bitcoin easier to buy, sell, and store for mainstream users.

events.title: Bitcoin Surpassed 100 Dollars
events.description: Bitcoin broke through the $100 barrier, reflecting the market's growing traction.

events.title: The Ethereum Whitepaper Was Published
events.description: Vitalik Buterin published the Ethereum whitepaper, proposing a blockchain for smart contracts and decentralized applications.

events.title: Dogecoin Was Launched
events.description: Dogecoin launched as a playful meme-inspired cryptocurrency and quickly gained a large online community.

events.title: Bitcoin Reached 1,000 Dollars
events.description: Bitcoin passed the $1,000 threshold, becoming a major milestone in mainstream awareness.

events.title: BitPay Expanded Merchant Adoption
events.description: BitPay increased cryptocurrency payment support for businesses, bolstering Bitcoin adoption.

events.title: The Monero Network Was Launched
events.description: Monero was introduced as a privacy-focused cryptocurrency using advanced cryptographic techniques.

events.title: Mt. Gox Was Hacked
events.description: Mt. Gox was compromised and lost a large share of customer funds, causing major shockwaves through the industry.

events.title: The Bitcoin Market Hit a Major Correction
events.description: The market experienced a sharp downturn after the early bull market phase, signaling volatility and maturation.

events.title: The Ethereum Development Network Expanded
events.description: The Ethereum ecosystem grew as developers and companies explored programmable blockchain applications.

events.title: The Ethereum Mainnet Was Launched
events.description: Ethereum's main network officially went live, enabling decentralized applications and smart contracts.

events.title: The Tether Project Emerged
events.description: Tether began to gain prominence as a stablecoin project designed to offer price stability relative to fiat currencies.

events.title: The Ethereum Ecosystem Continued Expanding
events.description: Applications and token projects began using Ethereum infrastructure at an accelerating pace.

events.title: The Bitcoin Halving of 2016 Took Place
events.description: Bitcoin's block subsidy was reduced in the 2016 halving event, affecting miner economics and market expectations.

events.title: The DAO Was Created on Ethereum
events.description: The DAO launched as one of the largest early decentralized autonomous organizations on Ethereum.

events.title: The DAO Attack Happened
events.description: A major vulnerability in The DAO led to the theft of a large amount of ETH, changing the trajectory of the Ethereum ecosystem.

events.title: Ethereum Hard Forked to Recover Funds
events.description: Ethereum was hard forked to reverse the DAO hack and restore stolen funds to affected investors.

events.title: Zcash Was Launched
events.description: Zcash launched as a privacy-focused cryptocurrency using zk-SNARKs for transaction confidentiality.

events.title: Bitcoin Reached 800 Dollars Again
events.description: The market exhibited notable volatility and recovery following the 2015-2016 slump.

events.title: The ICO Boom Exploded
events.description: Initial coin offerings became a major way for new blockchain projects to raise capital.

events.title: Bitcoin Surpassed 1,000 Dollars Again
events.description: Bitcoin resumed a strong upward trend as institutional and retail interest grew.

events.title: The Crypto Market Began a Major Bull Run
events.description: The market momentum accelerated as new investors entered the space at scale.

events.title: Segregated Witness Was Activated on Bitcoin
events.description: SegWit activated on Bitcoin, improving transaction scalability and paving the way for later features.

events.title: Bitcoin Reached 20,000 Dollars
events.description: Bitcoin hit a new historic high as the 2017 bull market reached full force.

events.title: Ethereum Passed 1,000 Dollars
events.description: Ethereum reached a major milestone, increasing attention on the smart contract ecosystem.

events.title: The Crypto Market Hit New Peaks
events.description: The market reached extraordinary valuation levels before entering a deeper correction.

events.title: The Crypto Market Corrected Sharply
events.description: Prices retrenched significantly as the market began a long-term downturn.

events.title: ICO Activity Slowed
events.description: Regulatory scrutiny and market weakness caused a major decline in ICO activity.

events.title: The SEC Warned Against ICO Misuse
events.description: United States regulators increased attention on ICOs and token sales.

events.title: The Crypto Market Entered a Long Bear Cycle
events.description: Bitcoin and other major cryptocurrencies entered a prolonged bear market as investor sentiment collapsed.

events.title: The Libra Project Was Announced
events.description: Facebook announced Libra, a blockchain-based payment project that sparked global regulatory debate.

events.title: The Crypto Market Reached New Lows
events.description: Many major cryptocurrencies traded at significant discounts compared to the 2017 highs.

events.title: The Market Began Stabilizing
events.description: After an extended downturn, investor sentiment gradually improved as the sector matured.

events.title: The Ethereum 2.0 Era Began to Take Form
events.description: The Ethereum ecosystem began preparing for the long-term shift from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake.

events.title: Bakkt Was Announced
events.description: Bakkt planned to provide regulated cryptocurrency infrastructure, including futures and custody services.

events.title: The DeFi Narrative Began to Form
events.description: Decentralized finance protocols gained increasing interest as a promising blockchain use case.

events.title: Bitcoin Reached 10,000 Dollars Again
events.description: Bitcoin regained a psychologically important level after an extended bear period.

events.title: Bitcoin Fell Sharply During Global Market Stress
events.description: The global pandemic intensified volatility across financial markets, including cryptocurrencies.

events.title: The 2020 Bitcoin Halving Took Place
events.description: Bitcoin's block reward halved again, reducing supply issuance and affecting market expectations.

events.title: DeFi Protocols Grew Rapidly
events.description: Decentralized lending, borrowing, and liquidity protocols began attracting significant capital.

events.title: Bitcoin Surged Above 10,000 Dollars
events.description: The market recovered strongly, helping Bitcoin re-enter a highly active bull cycle.

events.title: Institutional Crypto Adoption Kept Accelerating
events.description: Large investors and businesses increased their exposure to crypto assets and blockchain infrastructure.

events.title: The DeFi Ecosystem Expanded
events.description: The decentralized finance ecosystem grew in complexity, liquidity, and total value locked.

events.title: Bitcoin Began a New Bull Market
events.description: The market gained strong momentum, supported by institutional appetite and improved sentiment.

events.title: The Crypto Market Reached Historic Levels

events.title: Bitcoin Continued Its Strong Rally

events.title: The Crypto Industry Drew More Institutional Capital
events.description: Banks, funds, and large investors increased their exposure to blockchain-based assets and products.

events.title: The DeFi Market Continued Rising
events.description: Total value locked in DeFi protocols climbed sharply as new products gained traction.

events.title: The NFT Market Accelerated
events.description: Digital collectibles and blockchain art began attracting massive attention from collectors and creators.

events.title: The Stablecoin Market Expanded

events.title: Bitcoin Reached 60,000 Dollars Again
events.description: Bitcoin set a new cycle high as institutional and public interest intensified.

events.title: The Crypto Market Near $3 Trillion
events.description: The overall crypto market capitalization reached a historic level before a major pullback.

events.description: The sector suffered a major reset as trust, liquidity, and capital flows contracted.

events.description: Digital assets ended the year with improved liquidity, participation, and sentiment across major sectors.

events.description: Scaling technologies became central to the broader debate on transaction speed, cost, and network adoption.
